direction_as_read: Mixed: four small trials at the label's 40 mg report higher BMD against placebo; one larger trial giving 40 mg in milk found no significant effect
summary: One label, Calcium and Vitamin D with MBP, prints MBP 40 mg beside 600 mg calcium and 400 IU vitamin D, and states it supports bone. Four small placebo-controlled trials at 40 mg per day (17048062, 16133638, 12005077, 11388472, each 32 to 35 women) report higher BMD gain at different sites at P values near 0.04. The largest trial, 19296044 (84 women, 40 mg in milk), found no significant effect. No abstract names a primary outcome, and none measures fractures.
question_for_clinician: This is the closest case in the batch: 17048062 matches the label's 40 mg and purpose, with lumbar BMD 1.57% vs 0.13% (P = 0.042) and no primary outcome named. Agent recommendation: no credit, because BMD is a surrogate in healthy women, the trials are small, and the larger on-target trial 19296044 was null. Would full-text primary outcomes change your view?
